title: Dr. Owen Muir in the News
subtitle: I have a few media hits this week, and advice on how you can too!
body_html:
Dear readers—domain authority matters. My prior article on the topic was deeply flawed. However, we have a solution. If you don’t have enough domain authority—consider getting more authority. In my case, I did an interview with Authority Magazine on parenting:

Owen Muir Of Radial On How to Raise Children Who Feel Loved and Connected

Q:

We live in a world with incessant demands for our time and attention. There is so much distraction and disconnection. Can you share with our readers 5 steps that parents can take to help their children feel loved and connected? Please include examples or stories for each, if you can.

A:

1 . Checking — I ask my kids “did I get that right” at the end of a statement.

2 . Say “question mark” out loud: kids are bad at reading tone of voice. One way of solving this, that is a bit playful, is end your questions with the words “question mark.” They will laugh, but not miss the point.

3 . Take a not-knowing stance: “I am wondering if…” and “If I were you I might feel X, is that how you feel?” The more you don’t know — the better.

4 . Cool yourself down first!: When your emotions get hot, it’s always great to model cooling down for your kids. “I’m gonna take some deep breaths before we talk about this!”

5 . Correct your mistakes: when you get it wrong with your kids, admit it! Out loud, to them: “I misunderstood what you meant!”

In the same week, I also did an interview about AI use, in Medical News Today:

Frequent AI use linked to higher depression rates, study warns

MNT also reached out to Owen Muir, MD, DFAACAP, a psychiatrist at Radial, who echoed this sentiment. “If you wonder who would be more likely to talk to a Chatbot multiple times a day, that is selecting for people who are lonely, and more likely to be depressed.”

That sounds like an article people would want to read?! Also, I hope that means the robot audience will be more likely to trust what I have to say.

Keep writing, my friends. If you want to work with reporters, too, you can. Here is the link to “Help a Reporter Out.” This can help elevate your voice in the conversation (on the internet) as well. Remember—most reporters are on a tight deadline, so respond quickly to their questions, and try to stay out of the weeds.
